description: We are Nexora, a team of students passionate about space, technology, and solving real-world problems. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are working on the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Our team combines skills in coding, data analysis, UI/UX design, documentation, and presentation. We believe in teamwork, creativity, and learning together to build a meaningful and innovative solution.
summary:
SpectraShift is a space-data exploration platform designed to help researchers, students, and curious individuals investigate unusual astronomical candidates using data from NASA's SPHEREx mission.

The platform integrates publicly available astronomical datasets and scientific tools to support candidate detection, spectral analysis, and multi-epoch comparison. It processes SPHEREx observations, extracts photometric information, visualizes 102-band spectral data, and helps users examine changes in brightness and spectral characteristics over time.

By combining astronomical data processing, visualization, cross-matching, and candidate evaluation in one interactive environment, SpectraShift makes complex space-science workflows more accessible.

Our goal is not to claim the discovery of an unknown planet, but to provide an accessible research-oriented platform that helps users explore unusual astronomical candidates and investigate the unknown through real scientific data.
details:
SpectraShift is an interactive astronomical data exploration platform developed by Team Nexora_A for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, focusing on the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

The project uses publicly available NASA SPHEREx infrared spectral image data to explore unusual astronomical candidates. Its workflow combines astronomical image processing, photometric extraction, spectral visualization, multi-epoch comparison, and cross-matching with existing astronomical catalogs.

The platform is designed around the following workflow:

  1. Data Acquisition: Retrieve publicly available SPHEREx observations and relevant astronomical datasets.
  2. Data Processing: Work with FITS files using scientific image-processing techniques and astronomical Python libraries.
  3. Photometric Analysis: Extract source information and aperture-based photometric measurements using Astropy and Photutils.
  4. Visualization: Display astronomical images and spectral information through an interactive interface, including 102-band spectral exploration.
  5. Multi-Epoch Comparison: Compare observations from different times to investigate changes in source position, brightness, and spectral characteristics.
  6. Cross-Matching: Compare potential candidates against existing astronomical catalogs, including Gaia DR3 and SIMBAD.
  7. Candidate Evaluation: Apply filtering and scoring to help prioritize unusual sources for further investigation.

The project brings astronomical data retrieval, scientific processing, visualization, and candidate evaluation together in one accessible platform.

What makes SpectraShift different?

Instead of presenting astronomical data as disconnected files and complex scientific outputs, SpectraShift aims to transform them into an understandable and interactive exploration experience. It is designed for researchers, students, and general users who want to explore real astronomical observations.

The project identifies and evaluates potential candidates; it does not claim to have discovered Planet X or confirmed an unknown planet.
